eng-runtime

maya: Heads up — after the v7.0 rollout around 11:22 UTC we saw p95/p99 latency jump ~2.5-3x for a subset of hosts. Error rates stayed flat but throughput dropped on those hosts.
sam: Noticed this too. Correlates with an uptick in long-seq requests (>=1024 tokens) and a spike in KV cache miss rate on the same machines.
jordan: Rollback initiated for the canary group? Did we try switching to the prior tokenizer variant to confirm? :thinking:
maya: Yep, rolled the canary back to v6.9 at 11:38 — latency returned to baseline on those canary machines. Prod is still on v7.0 for ~80% traffic.
li: Quick profiling from one affected host attached. Seeing kernel selector flip to the slower attention kernel for ~30% of long calls, and batcher is forming smaller batches for seq>=1024 (batch size drop from 16->6). Logs:

```
[profile] seq_len=1024, selector=attn_v2_slow, batch_size=6, kv_cache_miss=0.42
[profile] seq_len=64, selector=attn_fast, batch_size=16, kv_cache_miss=0.03
```

This matches the observed per-token cost increase.

ops-bot: deploy-event: v7.0 rollout started 2026-03-17T11:20:00Z

sam: Two hypotheses: 1) Tokenizer change in v7.0 causes longer tokenization for some inputs -> longer seq distribution tail. 2) Model binary changes led to kernel misselection for moderate sequence lengths (512-1024).
maya: Also seeing KV cache eviction rate up ~3x on affected hosts (evict ops during prefix-heavy workloads). Could be memory pressure from different attention kernel memory layout.
jordan: Any noisy neighbor reports? Maybe another tenant spiking memory/IO causing eviction and smaller batches.
li: Checked host metrics — no obvious noisy tenant CPU hog, but one noisy shard had heavy memory fragmentation after the model load. Kernel memory allocator logs:

```
[allocator] host=host-23 mem_fragment=0.38 after mmap(model_v7)
[evict] reason=frag_threshold, freed=512MB
```

sam: Interesting. If allocator fragmentation causes frequent evictions, KV hits drop -> more recompute -> slower kernels -> batcher timeouts and smaller batches.
maya: Action items I propose:
1) Pause v7 rollout. (done for canary, request prod hold) 
2) Re-run tokenizer A/B: run v7 model with v6 tokenizer in a small canary to isolate tokenizer vs binary. 
3) Force kernel override to attn_fast for seq<=1024 on canaries to test selector hypothesis. 
4) Add a KV-cache eviction gauge to tracing and correlate with batch sizes.

jordan: I'll take item 3. Patching runtime config now: set kernel_select_override={"max_seq_fast":1024} for canary hosts.
li: I'll run a synthetic workload with heavy prefix reuse to exercise kv and measure eviction with and without the override.
sam: Also let's capture per-request tokenization length distribution before and after tokenizer swap. If tokenizer expands tokens for certain Unicode sequences in v7, that'll explain the tail.
maya: Good. If we confirm allocator fragmentation is root cause we should consider changing model mmap flags or pre-touch memory to reduce fragmentation on model load.

deploy-bot: note: rollback request sent to release manager for v7.0 canary -> awaiting approval

jordan: Patch applied on canary. Initial metrics after 10 minutes: selector stayed on attn_fast for most seq<=1024, batch sizes recovered to ~14, kv evict rate down 60% on canary hosts. Early p99 back to baseline.
li: Synthetic run shows tokenizer A/B: v7 tokenizer increases token counts by ~12% on our noisy corpus (emoji-heavy chat logs). That pushes many requests over 512->1024 boundary.
sam: So both things contributed: tokenizer shift increased seq-tail which exposed allocator+kernel selector fragility.
maya: Summary: tokenizer change moved distribution into region where kernel selection + allocator frag caused higher memory churn and evictions -> batching heuristics produced smaller batches -> overall p99 spike. Plan: revert tokenizer change in next patch, add selector guardrails, and improve allocator behavior on model load. I'll write a short postmortem and rollout checklist.

jordan: +1. Will collect the perf traces and a small reproducer for infra/alloc to debug memory fragmentation deeper.
li: I'll add the KV eviction gauge and a per-host token_len histogram to the console dashboards.
maya: Thanks all — nice quick triage. :raised_hands:
